A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GRACE. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and complete Appendices A–E support reliable comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v5.

before.justification: v3 reports original distillation and quantization benchmarks, component ablations, deployment measurements, qualitative analyses and controller simulations.

after.justification: v5 retains these empirical results and adds Qwen3-VL evaluation, sequential quantization comparisons, gating experiments and attention analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3.4 replaces initialization from the 99th percentile of absolute weights with an MSE-minimizing search over 20 candidate scales. This changes a localized quantization step; confidence-gated DKD, RCKA and the adaptive controller retain their underlying procedures.

E1.justification: Table 7 adds evaluations on DocVQA and MathVista, absent from v3. ShareGPT4V training data and the earlier benchmarks remain. The added Qwen3-VL evaluation uses previously represented benchmarks.

E2.justification: Table 7 adds GRACE-distillation-followed-by-GPTQ and GRACE-distillation-followed-by-AWQ as alternatives to joint QAT+KD. Appendix C.3 adds standard KD to the new attention comparisons. Comparator membership in retained Tables 1, 2 and 5 is unchanged.

E3.justification: v5 adds Qwen3-VL 8B-to-2B configurations, a standard-KL gating-function/coefficient sweep and sequential distillation-then-PTQ testing. Appendix D.1 changes the stated controller target from 0.35 to 3.0, initial beta from 1.0 to 0.5 and bounds from [0.1, 5.0] to [0.1, 1.0]. Table 8 and D.2 retain the old values, leaving the actual settings and any reruns unresolved.

E4.justification: New Figure 6 tests gating functions and coefficient sensitivity. Appendix A.3 tests whether post-distillation PTQ can substitute for joint training. Appendix C.3 adds three multilayer attention comparisons among baseline, standard KD and GRACE. These substantially extend the retained component ablations and qualitative analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions retain deployment averaging over unspecified multiple runs and the same controller simulation tolerance band. v5 adds no seed information, explicit repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: Retained Tables 1–5 have unchanged scores, but substantial results are added. Table 6 reports Qwen3-VL averages of 76.7, 75.9 and 75.0 for GRACE BF16, INT8 and INT4, versus a 67.3 baseline. Table 7 reports joint INT4 averaging 63.6 versus 60.9/60.5 after GRACE followed by GPTQ/AWQ. Gating and attention findings are also newly reported.

T1.justification: Section 3.4 replaces the mathematical scale-initialization rule with an explicit MSE argmin and revises the optimization equation to update log-scales. The covariance theorem, variational KL bound, formal assumptions and Appendix B proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central claims remain an IB-based joint distillation/QAT framework using confidence gating, relational alignment and adaptive control, with INT4 models exceeding BF16 baselines while providing approximately threefold throughput and 54% memory reduction. The rewritten introduction and conclusion retain this scope.

C2.justification: v5 adds explanations of hard gating discarding useful supervision and sequential PTQ losing knowledge that joint training preserves. The conclusion explicitly discusses teacher dependency and offline training cost, plus possible activation-quantization instability. Earlier image-text coverage and video/audio extension boundaries remain.

D1.justification: v5 newly states code/data availability and specifies the scale-search interval, a separate scale optimizer group, zero scale weight decay and a tenfold scale learning rate. Section 4 changes training hardware from eight GH200s to eight H100s, while Appendix D still specifies GH200s, introducing a reproducibility inconsistency.

R1.justification: New Appendix E.4 discusses multimodal reasoning, editing and structured generation, citing MMErroR, ChordEdit, Render-in-the-Loop, VAnim and CABM. Additional introduction and Qwen3-VL references appear, while Kolchinsky et al. is removed. The central positioning relative to KD, QAT and IB remains.

P1.justification: The introduction, quantization section, ablation discussion and conclusion undergo substantial rewriting. New appendix subsections, explicit limitations, acknowledgements and disclosure text expand the narrative; affiliation and conference front matter also change.

P2.justification: Figure 1 changes from a Qwen2-VL radar chart to a LLaVA throughput–accuracy–memory comparison, and Figure 4 is substantially redrawn. v5 adds the gating figure, three attention figures and two experimental tables. Retained appendix figures are also relocated or resized.

improvement.justification: v5 strengthens validation through gating tests, sequential-PTQ comparisons and Qwen3-VL results, while adding implementation information and explicit limitations. However, v3's consistent controller settings become contradictory between v5 Appendix D.1 and Table 8/D.2, and training hardware also conflicts between sections. These regressions obscure reproduction of the central training procedure. The useful new evidence and reduced reproducibility leave the net quality direction uncertain.
